findings.summary: apps/api/package.json declared @music-os-360/types and @music-os-360/ai-skills via file:../../packages/X instead of workspace:* (apps/web already used the correct convention). Proven via 'pnpm turbo build --dry=json' before/after: api#build/typecheck/test's dependencies array was [] (empty) with file:, meaning turbo never serialized these packages' build order relative to apps/api at all -- a pure race, previously masked by turbo cache hits (once packages/types was cached from any prior run, its dist/ already existed on disk). This mission's pnpm-lock.yaml changes (Cluster B, dependency-advisory remediation) forced a full cache invalidation, which is what first exposed the race in CI: TypeCheck and Build jobs both failed nondeterministically with 'Cannot find module @music-os-360/types', unreproducible locally on a fast machine after the same cold-cache clear.
findings.justification: Fixed: both dependencies switched to workspace:* in apps/api/package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml refreshed (resolved 'version' unchanged -- link:../../packages/X both before and after, only the specifier protocol differs). turbo --dry=json confirms api#build/typecheck/test now correctly depend on ai-skills#build+types#build. Full cold-cache 'pnpm turbo build typecheck' (12/12 tasks) and both apps' direct tsc typecheck pass.

findings.summary: Independently confirmed (read-only re-audit): server/ai-proxy.ts is a standalone http server (not part of apps/api's NestJS auth stack) exposing POST /api/ai/generate (raw OpenAI passthrough, billed to OPENAI_API_KEY) and POST /api/acrcloud/:endpoint with zero authentication, zero tenant scoping, zero rate limiting, and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every response (line 131). Confirmed exhaustively unreferenced: no docker-compose/Dockerfile/package.json script/workflow starts this process, and apps/web has 0 callers of /api/ai/generate -- not a live production vulnerability today, but a real footgun if ever started manually. Already documented in docs/NAMING_NORMALIZATION_CANONICAL_MAP.md (2026-09-24 entry); recorded here for this independent security-audit pass's own evidence trail. Grep for Access-Control-Allow-Origin.*\* repo-wide confirms this is the ONLY file with a wildcard-CORS pattern.
findings.justification: server/ai-proxy.ts confirmed HIGH-severity by design (zero auth, wildcard CORS, OPENAI_API_KEY-billed passthrough) but exhaustively confirmed unreachable in current deployment: zero references in any docker-compose*.yml, either Dockerfile, any package.json script, or .github/workflows/**, and zero frontend callers. Not fixed because the two real remediations (delete the file, or harden it to match the backend's real auth/tenancy model) both require a product/eng decision on whether this file is still needed for some undocumented deployment target -- a naming/audit mission cannot answer that unilaterally. Fully documented with the exact decision question in docs/NAMING_NORMALIZATION_CANONICAL_MAP.md (2026-09-24 entry). Accepted as known debt pending that decision, not silently ignored.

findings.summary: RLS census across all 274 migrations (up()-only event extraction, resolving templated for-loop table lists and quoted ${table} refs): 171 currently-existing application tables (CREATE TABLE minus real DROP TABLE minus rename-swap artifacts, event-ordered). 178 distinct table names have a confirmed ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY event with no later DISABLE in up(). Diff (current tables with zero RLS-enable event) = 3 initial candidates, all resolved as non-issues on manual read: skill_run_logs and workflow_execution_logs DO have RLS (apps/api/src/database/migrations/20260613000013_RlsPoliciesSkillWorkflowLogs.ts:45, missed by regex because the for-loop destructures a tuple array, not a bare table var); market_reference_metrics is deliberately tenant-less (no tenant_id column, documented cross-tenant public-data cache, apps/api/src/database/migrations/20260831000003_CreateMarketReferenceMetrics.ts:15-25). Zero real tenant-scoped tables found missing RLS.
findings.justification: Real RLS census across all 274 migrations found zero tenant-scoped tables missing RLS. 3 initial diff candidates all resolved as non-issues on manual read (2 false-negatives from a regex extraction blind spot, both tables confirmed to have real RLS; 1 deliberately tenant-less public-data-cache table by design). findings.summary: entities.ts <-> migrations schema-drift guard coverage is narrow, not exhaustive. Found: (1) a generic migrations/index.ts registry-parity guard (scripts/verify-migration-source-of-truth.mjs) that DOES cover 100% of migration files deterministically; but (2) no equivalent exhaustive guard for entities.ts @Column declarations vs actual physical columns -- coverage is a set of per-incident targeted specs (apps/api/src/database/lead-entity-schema-alignment.spec.ts, client-entity-schema-alignment.spec.ts, work-participants-normalization.spec.ts, form-field-dto-parity.spec.ts, plus migration-specific specs for create-client-attachments/restore-ecad/remove-legacy-society-code) written reactively after a real drift bug (e.g. leads.score/pipeline_stage). apps/api/test/e2e/schema/schema-reconciliation.e2e-spec.ts is a real live-Postgres e2e test but only exercises 5 of ~171 current tables (conversations, conversation_messages, transactions, financial_categories, leads) via reflect-metadata + actual repo.save/find calls -- TypeORM's synchronize:false does not validate unqueried entities' columns at DataSource.initialize(). A future ad-hoc column addition/removal on entities.ts for any of the other ~165 tables would not be caught pre-runtime by any existing guard. Spot-checked apps/api/src/database/entities.ts InvoiceEntity (lines 1061-1121) against the most recent migration touching that table (20260923000001_RenameInvoiceTomadorGenericFieldsToEnglish.ts) and found zero drift (tomador_address/tomador_city already correct in entities.ts) -- no live bug found, this finding is about missing systemic coverage, not a confirmed current drift instance.
findings.justification: Real audit confirmed the schema-reconciliation e2e guard exercises only 5 of ~171 current tables via live-Postgres repo.save/find calls; entities.ts<->migration drift is otherwise caught only by per-incident targeted specs written reactively after real bugs. Spot-checked InvoiceEntity against its most recent migration and found zero drift -- no active bug exists today. Not expanded to full 171-table coverage in this pass: building an exhaustive live-Postgres schema-reconciliation harness for every table is a real, scoped engineering task warranting its own review, not an incidental fix. Accepted as known coverage debt, documented in docs/NAMING_NORMALIZATION_CANONICAL_MAP.md's audit trail.
